formulations.Polymer system Notes: Random EO-PO copolymer (EO:PO = 84:16 molar), made with partially hydrolyzed organoaluminum catalyst. Undoped copolymer: Tg 200 K, Tm 311 K (Table 1).
formulations.Notes: LiI at 10 mol% relative to EO units (Li:EO = 0.1). Li:monomer and Li:functional group (0.084) were calculated over all EO+PO units, each with one ether O. Tg 226 K, no Tm listed (Table 1). Text says iodide complexes are thermally stable at higher T but have RT conductivity about one order of magnitude lower than LiBF4. Conductivity is only in Fig. 1; its digitised table has an implausible axis (positive log sigma), so conductivity is left null.
formulations.Reference: J. Przyłuski, W. Wieczorek, Solid State Ionics 53-56 (1992) 1071-1076

formulations.Polymer system Notes: Random EO-PO copolymer (EO:PO = 84:16 molar). Undoped copolymer: Tg 200 K, Tm 311 K.
formulations.Notes: LiClO4 at 10 mol% relative to EO units (Li:EO = 0.1); the ratios were calculated over EO+PO units. Tg 236 K, no Tm in Table 1. However, the text says the system is not thermally stable above the Tm of the crystalline phase (311 K). With Li electrodes the high-frequency semicircle in the impedance vanishes above the copolymer Tm (Fig. 7, 293 K). No passive layer was seen over several days at 303 K. Fig. 1 digitisation is implausible, so conductivity is null.
formulations.Reference: J. Przyłuski, W. Wieczorek, Solid State Ionics 53-56 (1992) 1071-1076

formulations.Notes: LiBF4 at 1 mol% (assumed relative to EO units, as in Fig. 1); the ratios were calculated over EO+PO units. Tg 216 K, Tm 314 K (Table 1). Fig. 3 conductivities at 288/303 K are not used because the digitised x positions (2, 4, 6... mol%) do not match the stated compositions.
formulations.Reference: J. Przyłuski, W. Wieczorek, Solid State Ionics 53-56 (1992) 1071-1076

formulations.Notes: LiBF4 at 3 mol% (assumed relative to EO); the ratios were calculated over EO+PO units. Tg 216 K, Tm 311 K (Table 1). Fig. 3 conductivity is not used because the digitised x positions are uncertain.
formulations.Reference: J. Przyłuski, W. Wieczorek, Solid State Ionics 53-56 (1992) 1071-1076

formulations.Notes: LiBF4 at 5 mol% (assumed relative to EO); the ratios were calculated over EO+PO units. Tg 208 K, Tm 306 K (Table 1), the lowest Tm; the authors suggest a eutectic near this composition. This composition gave the highest conductivity. Text says it exceeded 1e-4 S/cm at 303 K (Fig. 3; digitised max about 10^-4.0), but no exact value is given, so the field is left null.
formulations.Reference: J. Przyłuski, W. Wieczorek, Solid State Ionics 53-56 (1992) 1071-1076

formulations.Notes: LiBF4 at 10 mol% relative to EO units (Li:EO = 0.1); the ratios were calculated over EO+PO units. Tg 208 K, Tm 309 K (Table 1). It had the highest RT conductivity among the salts in Fig. 1 (range 1e-5 to 1e-4 at RT, 1e-3 to 1e-2 at 373 K for all salts). It is not thermally stable above Tm. The Fig. 1 digitisation is implausible. Fig. 3 digitised values (about 10^-4.6 at 15 C and 10^-4.3 at 30 C) are not entered because they are unverified.
formulations.Reference: J. Przyłuski, W. Wieczorek, Solid State Ionics 53-56 (1992) 1071-1076

formulations.Notes: LiBF4 at 15 mol% (assumed relative to EO); the ratios were calculated over EO+PO units. Tg 217 K, no Tm (Table 1).
formulations.Reference: J. Przyłuski, W. Wieczorek, Solid State Ionics 53-56 (1992) 1071-1076

formulations.Notes: LiBF4 at 20 mol% (assumed relative to EO); the ratios were calculated over EO+PO units. Tg 214 K, no Tm (Table 1). A second conductivity maximum appears at about 20 mol% (Fig. 3); no exact values are given.

formulations.Notes: LiBF4 at 50 mol% (assumed relative to EO); the ratios were calculated over EO+PO units. Shown only in Fig. 3, with no DSC data. Digitised Fig. 3 values (about 10^-6.4 S/cm at 15 C and 10^-5.9 at 30 C) are not entered because they cannot be checked against the text.

formulations.Polymer system Notes: Aliphatic polysulfone from free-radical copolymerization of SO2 with allyl alcohol at 195 or 273 K (t-butyl hydroperoxide initiator).
formulations.Notes: LiClO4 at 10 mol% relative to copolymer molecular units. Text: RT conductivity does not exceed 1e-8 S/cm, and the system is thermally stable up to 373 K (Fig. 4). Values from the digitised plot are not entered.
formulations.Reference: J. Przyłuski, W. Wieczorek, Solid State Ionics 53-56 (1992) 1071-1076

formulations.Polymer system Notes: Aliphatic polysulfone from free-radical copolymerization of SO2 with vinyl acetate.
formulations.Notes: LiClO4 at 10 mol% relative to copolymer molecular units. Text gives order-of-magnitude conductivity: about 1e-6 S/cm at RT rising to about 1e-5 S/cm at 373 K, roughly two orders higher than AA-SO2 (Fig. 4). No precise values are given, so the fields are left null.
formulations.Reference: J. Przyłuski, W. Wieczorek, Solid State Ionics 53-56 (1992) 1071-1076

formulations.Polymer system Notes: Aliphatic polysulfone from free-radical copolymerization of SO2 with acrylamide.
formulations.Notes: LiClO4 at 10 mol% relative to copolymer molecular units. Text: RT conductivity exceeds 1e-5 S/cm, about ten times higher than PEO-LiClO4, and the system is thermally stable up to 373 K (Fig. 4). No exact values are given; the digitised plot is not used.
formulations.Reference: J. Przyłuski, W. Wieczorek, Solid State Ionics 53-56 (1992) 1071-1076

formulations.Polymer system Notes: Aliphatic polysulfite from ionic copolymerization of SO2 with EO at room temperature (random copolymer). The undoped copolymer is amorphous.
formulations.Notes: LiBF4 at 10 mol% relative to copolymer monomeric units. Text: ambient conductivity exceeds 1e-6 S/cm, and the system is thermally stable up to almost 373 K (Fig. 5). The system is not stable over time. No exact values are given.
formulations.Reference: J. Przyłuski, W. Wieczorek, Solid State Ionics 53-56 (1992) 1071-1076

formulations.Polymer system Notes: Aliphatic polysulfite from ionic copolymerization of SO2 with EO (random copolymer). The undoped copolymer is amorphous.
formulations.Notes: LiClO4 at 10 mol% relative to copolymer monomeric units. The salt forms a crystalline complex with a high heat of melting (Fig. 6 DSC). Fig. 6 labels events at 229 K (probably Tg, not entered), 312 K (melting peak, entered as Tm 38.85 C) and 382 K; peak assignment is by inference. Text: ambient conductivity exceeds 1e-6 S/cm (Fig. 5). The system is not stable over time and needs PEO blending.
formulations.Reference: J. Przyłuski, W. Wieczorek, Solid State Ionics 53-56 (1992) 1071-1076
